name: Kodobane's Head
summary: Near the Forgotten Pools, Barak Kodobane's severed head proves the cunning chieftain's death. The orc warlord Regthar Deathgate receives it as proof that the centaur threat there has been broken.

sections.title: A Trophy of War
sections.body: Kolkar bands in the Barrens have long been divided, but ambitious warlords now threaten to gather them into an army. Barak Kodobane made his camp by the lush waters of the Forgotten Pools, where the oasis offers vital resources and nearby paths lie open to raids. Regthar Deathgate, stationed in a bunker west of the Crossroads, demands Kodobane's severed head as proof that this commander can no longer rally his kin against the Horde.

faq.answer: Barak Kodobane was a prominent chieftain among the Kolkar centaur. Cunning and commanding where many of his kin were undisciplined, he organized warbands and camped around the Forgotten Pools to assert Kolkar dominance over the northern Barrens.

faq.q: Why does Regthar Deathgate want his head?
faq.answer: Regthar Deathgate is tasked with securing Horde territory in the Barrens. The centaur are usually fractious, so leaders with tactical vision are singled out. Regthar demands Kodobane's head to make certain the chieftain is dead, not merely displaced.
Barak Kodobane camps near the Forgotten Pools, the northern oasis just northwest of the Crossroads in the Barrens.

faq.q: Does killing Barak stop the Kolkar threat?
faq.answer: No. Barak Kodobane is the first of several warlords rallying the Kolkar. His death disrupts their presence at the Forgotten Pools, but Verog the Dervish and Hezrul Bloodmark continue to direct centaur aggression across the Barrens.

angles.text: For generations, the centaur drove the nomadic tauren across Kalimdor to the brink of extinction. Killing Barak Kodobane avenges centuries of bloodshed and protects the pastures of Mulgore and the Barrens.
The Barrens crossroads link Orgrimmar and Thunder Bluff by land. Suppressing centaur leaders like Kodobane helps keep caravan trails safe.
